headline: A useful next hypothesis needs two still-live protected obligations with a resource-order conflict. More travel on the same serial reuse chain did not create that condition. Test whether earlier real supply can pay a later detour that avoids harming the other obligation; do not call this established MPC/LNS functionality a new method.

scope.target: Actual R1 release -> actual cross-owner R2 resource use -> later R1 needed for a strictly better all-job-protected result, followed separately by same-information strong-method comparison and complete-request timing.
not_claimed: native feasibility of the proposed embedding
general impossibility of the old domain
statistically held-out validation of the existing predictor
scope.no_new_study_admitted: This is a design and stop-rule proposal, not a frozen numeric native protocol. The existing 256 discovery negative remains closed and its 256 validation cells remain unexecuted.

historical_diagnosis.finding: The gate6 1.410 model gain is matched by ordinary plateau coordinate search. Neutral paths already remove the apparent strict-coordinate barrier. A comparison against strict descent alone would be weak.

The late Storage gate equalizes the donor release that the initial detour was supposed to improve. Earlier receiver service removes later overlap. In the finite tested cells, plateau coordinate, pair repair and enumeration match. This is a timing-structure diagnosis, not a separability theorem.

All192 actual branches complete five jobs, but selected-action assessment remains174 assessed/18 unknown; only5/12 initial families are complete. The complete block1_load2 comparison improves total completion by4.099999999999994 with later_action=native_default. A separate real coupled subcube exists, but has protected coordinate improvements and does not establish method necessity.

The actual60 online study retains52 assessed/8 unknown. Four search methods and later-default ablation produce the same five-job outcome in all six cases. Only two complete fixed-window families support the roughly4.1 comparison. Six initial unknowns are common model-admission refusal, not asymmetric owner information; two later unknowns remain.

All256 discovery projections and64 factorial cubes are retained: no strict-protection barrier and no projected necessary chain. Ordinary strict coordinate reaches all eight finite optima. Sixteen initial-only regret cubes already harm the completed loaded obligation, so later routing cannot repair them. This closed negative is not a reason to append more parameter values.

The withdrawn400s contrast and the eight saturated P5 domains are excluded as new evidence. The new mechanism below changes the causal resource structure, not the labels or interpretation of these results.

anchors: no hidden stock or omitted blocker obligation
source_explanation.finding: P supplies independent initial node1 occupancy, but its only job ends at sink9. It cannot remain a later competing unfinished obligation at node3. There is a real early blocker, not a second later protected traffic chain.

Only L has two empty returns and two loaded reuses. The controlled later choice is only the first reuse at7; the second return is immediate and second loaded reuse requests3. E supplies one receiver and remains at4. Thus the same donor chain carries most downstream gains and the finite assignment freedom is small.

A granted R2 acquires a real receiving lease, moves an existing tray, and only EMPTY_RECEIVED invokes loading. The model counts stationary, incoming and leased presence with OR semantics per tray. Earlier release is not supply until this chain executes. Storage handling is specialized to job 'loaded', so the proposed new P lifecycle is outside the current supported model and cannot be admitted by merely changing its guard.

An installed preference is neither a forced wait nor a reserved route. S4 ranks all candidates; a legal preference changes the score only while allowed, and committed incoming occupancy precedes EDGE_ENTER. A proposed conflict must be defined from reservation/lease through actual release, not just the movement receipt. Final unload writes a business completion; later choices never rewrite an already completed job.

Searches share32 initial and4 later alternatives; plateau exploration includes neutral moves and all final candidates undergo exact per-job screening. A protection barrier only challenges this protected-intermediate neighborhood. Ordinary MPC or LNS may internally explore an unprotected partial proposal and then deploy a protected complete result; such exploration must not be artificially prohibited to manufacture superiority.

one_new_hypothesis.name: Supply advancement and later corridor avoidance for two live protected obligations
one_new_hypothesis.statement: A donor R1 improvement can release L early enough for a genuine A6->B7 transfer. If the resulting Q=reuse1 would then reserve a capacity-one corridor before a different still-live protected job X, the early transfer can delay X. A legal later bypass can remove that conflict, but costs Q additional travel. The coupled R2/bypass is useful when the real advancement is sufficient to pay that extra cost, whereas a bypass under the incumbent supply window cannot preserve Q. The second protected job must remain unfinished at this decision; a completed-prefix loss cannot be paid back.
one_new_hypothesis.important_limit: This does not require later R1 for every possible positive gain: earlier donor R1 alone may already improve its own job. The test is whether allowing later R1 yields a strictly better complete protected result than the strongest same-domain later-default and fixed-initial families, and whether that extra improvement requires the actual cross-owner transfer.
minimal_topology_embedding_draft: Use a separate new five-job/three-tray synthetic contract. Keep the original five protected identities and all old study inputs unchanged. Keep all methods on the same new graph, jobs, capacities, FIFO, wire delays and stock.

Instead of terminating blocker P at9, give that same still-live job a declared mandatory on-carrier stage at9 and a later destination reached through shared corridor3. One concrete topology draft is new9->3 plus3->10 to a new finite private exit10. Node9 remains finite and does not export empty trays. The release/dwell is a public obligation of P, not a controller pause or a gate on L.

All added directed edges are equally available to every permitted tray. They cannot be labelled P-only. Their effects on native S4 potentials and autonomous alternatives, including1->9 for other loaded traffic, must be modeled and audited. If these alternatives make the old default achieve the same result, the hypothesis fails.

The separate exit prevents an artificial permanently parked tray at shared3 from turning the comparison into an unfinished-job trick. All five jobs and both L reuses must finish and be screened. Every occupancy at4/6 and downstream headway still matters.

Use an incumbent absolute public first-return window b and an alternative request at the first actually observed empty opportunity. Submit only after local ownership/availability/delivered-demand checks. An absolute window lets early donor R1 alone leave Q's timing unchanged; it does not permit a premature transfer of a still-loaded or foreign tray.

This draft requires a new per-job Storage-capable public predictor and fresh strict input guards; the current initial/later predictor explicitly does not support it. No native API or permission extension is proposed. No numeric instance is asserted feasible here.

definitions.t0: Baseline Q admission time to the capacity-one conflicting resource, measured from the first irreversible reservation that counts against its capacity.
definitions.x: Independent X admission time to the same resource in the baseline.
definitions.HQ_HX: Exact effective conflicting reservation/occupancy/headway durations for Q and X, including incoming edges and the actual release event. These are not just node service times.
definitions.D: t0-x, with baseline X fully clear before Q: D>=HX>0.
definitions.s: Largest lawful advance of Q's resource admission under early donor release plus earlier R2, after all message/load/travel epochs; it must be derived from the public causal model, not set from a favorable native result.
definitions.delta: Additional Q completion time of the bypass relative to its uncontested normal suffix, including different service/headway effects; constant only in the explicitly isolated resource-order abstraction.
definitions.m: Maximum Q advancement available to the entire fixed-initial-route family under the same legal transfer windows, not just one selected fixed control.

sufficient_interval_conditions_for_the_i: s-delta>D-HX. This extra inequality is essential: merely paying the detour does not prove improvement over the best safe ordinary timing.
The bypass avoids every resource whose use would delay X, and has no unmodeled conflict with any other protected obligation.

The default native scorer still selects the normal corridor whenever the analytical argument assumes it. If native_default itself switches to the bypass, count that as a successful ablation and reject necessity.
Earlier donor release itself preserves its completed job; the transfer retains the same real L identity and no replacement tray can supply Q before the certified bound.
The route command can execute before commitment with current receiving permission and unchanged generation/traversal; a later ACK marked updated alone is insufficient.
short_derivation: For an ordinary-route advancement a<=D, X reaches the contested resource no later than Q. Because X must clear first, Q's protected advancement is at most D-HX.

For D<a<=s<D+HQ, Q reserves first but still holds conflicting capacity when X would enter. X is delayed. At the equality boundary the native event order must be checked; it cannot produce a larger safe bound than X-first service.

For the bypass at advance s, Q gains s-delta while X's conflict is removed. With s-delta>D-HX, it beats every protected timing-only outcome in this isolated one-resource interval, not merely a coarse chosen window.

Under unchanged initial R1, at most m<delta advance is available; the bypass would regress Q. Under the delayed R2 window it also regresses Q. Thus early donor availability and the actual transfer matter to paying this bypass, while X's still-live resource conflict makes a later change relevant.

This is a conditional analytic screen, not a theorem about the full G31 network. Multiple receiving leases, downstream calendars, scorer changes, queue order, message lead time or another tray invalidate the reduction unless explicitly bounded.
analytical_screen_before_any_parameter_g.construction_rule: Before evaluating outcomes, derive an admissible interval for the independent P release and bypass duration from public travel/service/communication bounds and the inequalities. Choose one deterministic interior value only if the interval is nonempty and all native action lead-time conditions hold; record an empty interval as a failed hypothesis. No outcome-driven widening, successive extra delays or appended grid. Any numerical validation instance must be preregistered separately from this analytical construction.

one_new_hypothesis.why_this_differs_from_the_closed_256_neg: That study only changed later travel while P still disappeared into sink9. This draft retains a different unfinished protected obligation through the later resource conflict, and asks for an actual change in resource order. The L release is not equalized by a Storage gate. It remains a new synthetic mechanism hypothesis, not an improvement to the original airport contract.
falsification_and_claim_levels: Stop before simulation if the public inequalities, source-authority coverage or command lead-time interval are empty/unknown.
Stop the necessity claim if any completed-prefix job regresses, any job remains unfinished, any required route is rejected/stale/no-effect, or later-default has the same best protected vector.

Require the actual chain: original R1 EDGE_ENTER difference -> loaded unload/hold release -> same L departed/received A6->B7 with target lease/occupancy -> Q load -> later actual bypass -> X capacity no longer delayed. Distinguish reservation publication from actual EDGE_ENTER.

Use common-input counterfactuals with donor route held, R2 window held and later preference withheld. No-op means retain native behavior, never forced next3. A transfer rejected or executed with another tray cannot establish this chain.

Keep full fixed-initial family with all four E windows, both return rules and both later routes. Compare full later-default family, not a single ablation action. All32 initial/four later candidates remain in the denominator; budget, infeasible, no-effect and unknown are separate.

Give strict coordinate, plateau coordinate, pair repair, ordinary receding-horizon enumeration and a boundary-aware repair reference the same observations/actions/total evaluation or wall budget. Record all neutral protected paths. A resource-order/temporal-dependency comparator should get the same valid switch groups, not a weaker ETA surrogate.

A coupled protected witness would establish mechanism existence only. Equality with MPC/LNS/coordinate means no new optimizer advantage. Even a protected-intermediate coordinate barrier does not prove that ordinary algorithms cannot find the complete proposal.

No new result from this designed case is held-out. Future validation must use a separate frozen unseen configuration or exogenous realization, include both overlap-absent and insufficient-advance negatives, and not be read while constructing this case. The old unexecuted validation256 is not silently repurposed.

primary_sources.title: An Integrated Model Predictive Scheme for Baggage-Handling Systems: Routing, Line Balancing, and Empty-Cart Management
primary_sources.authors: Y. Zeinaly, B. De Schutter, H. Hellendoorn
primary_sources.inspected: Author report15-019, II-A assumptions A2-A4; III receding horizon and objective
primary_sources.relevance_and_difference: Joint loaded routing and empty management with repeated first-action execution are established. The flow approximation, sampled travel and omission of unloading queues under sufficient-capacity assumptions do not supply an exact finite-tray, per-job no-regression proof. Our proposed conflict explicitly retains finite receiving occupancy and individual jobs.

primary_sources.title: Integrated Task Assignment and Path Planning for Capacitated Multi-Agent Pickup and Delivery
primary_sources.inspected: IV-B-D marginal completion-related insertion, regret, path updates and anytime destroy/reinsert
primary_sources.relevance_and_difference: Coupled collision-aware assignment and routing already use completion-related costs and repair. A strong comparator must account for actual service obligations, not nearest-empty arrival alone. The proposed G31 fixture has far less assignment freedom; an advantage from hiding alternative trays or repair moves would not be a meaningful comparison.

primary_sources.title: Large Neighborhood Search for Multi-Agent Task Assignment and Path Finding with Precedence Constraints
primary_sources.inspected: 4.2-4.5 successor closure, boundary retiming, regret/MAPF-PC repair and validation
primary_sources.relevance_and_difference: Successor closure and repair of invalidated exterior paths are established. Cross-resource dependencies and per-job protection would be additional G31 contracts to preserve, not a novelty claim for closure itself. This is the inspected preprint version; no acceptance claim.

primary_sources.title: Predictive Control for Baggage Handling Systems Using Mixed Integer Linear Programming
primary_sources.inspected: 2.1 first-action receding horizon;3.1 simplified vertical queues and sampled travel;4.2 warm start
primary_sources.relevance_and_difference: Rolling execution and warm starts are ordinary references. Real-valued queue approximations and sampled travel cannot replace exact native FIFO, finite carriers, real wire time or the current strict per-job test.

primary_sources.title: Receding Horizon Re-ordering of Multi-Agent Execution Schedules
primary_sources.authors: Berndt, van Duijkeren, Palmieri, Kleiner, Keviczky
primary_sources.inspected: Introduction;IV SADG;V-D grouping;VI finite-horizon subset and recursive feasibility
primary_sources.relevance_and_difference: The paper changes execution order while spatial routes remain fixed, using a switchable dependency graph and MILP. Its acyclicity/recursive-feasibility argument assumes its own execution model. G31 cannot directly flip another owner's reservation order; only lawful route/transfer intents can induce a change. Minimizing total route completion also does not imply every job is no worse.

primary_sources.title: Bidirectional Temporal Plan Graph: Enabling Switchable Passing Orders for More Efficient Multi-Agent Path Finding Plan Execution
primary_sources.inspected: 2.1-2.2 model/execution;4 switching and adversarial execution-time example;5 grouping
primary_sources.relevance_and_difference: Safe flexibility in passing order is already studied. The paper explicitly gives an adversarial case where more flexible execution takes longer; safety does not imply per-job protection. Its following-conflict/onboard-avoidance assumptions cannot be imported to weaken G31 capacity/headway. Existing completed or in-progress prefixes remain fixed.

primary_sources.title: Speedup Techniques for Switchable Temporal Plan Graph Optimization
primary_sources.inspected: TPG earliest-arrival longest paths;4.2 full edge grouping;5 incremental implementation
primary_sources.relevance_and_difference: Grouped dependency changes and incremental longest-path updates are established computational techniques. For a fixed acyclic order graph, longest paths compute earliest times efficiently. A G31 reduction must also encode changing route choice, leases, capacity/FIFO, delayed ACK and native tie order; simply substituting a DAG evaluator would not preserve the current model.
